hypothesis: The project's hypothesis: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. This run tests no part of it. It asks one question of the instrument every step of a correction loop pays for: whether the recorder writes each answer's files with the bytes it writes today, in less time, when the engine's scheduler copies each wanted output on the card's own queue and waits for the card once a split, and not once at each of the 212 outputs a token.
why_this_direction: Steps 1 and 2 of the method are the overlaps of the full traces, and step 5 measures the computation again on the current model's own answers after every update: each such measurement is the engine's capture of the thirty fitting answers, and under Astra's choice of November 15 that capture is the measured loss at every step. The capture is about three quarters of a gradient step as priced (223 s of about 4.5 minutes; speed review, 'A step taken by the gradient'), and the recorder's generation is nearly all of the capture. Two ways to shorten the generation with its bytes kept have been measured and closed: the recorder's own bookkeeping is 2.2 to 2.4 ms of a kept token (speed review, 'The recorder's own bookkeeping, and two recorders on one card'), and two or three recorder processes side by side write the solo's bytes at 0.72 of one process's answers a second (runs/recorders-beside-original/result.json, which named what is left: the engine's own work at each token). The recorder-modes record of November 14 says where a token goes: 7.9 ms is the plain decode with its scores, 9.9 to 13.4 with the scheduler's stops at every kept output and nothing read, 14.2 to 15.6 with the read-back and the records. The installed scheduler computes up to each wanted output, waits for the card, and lets the recorder read it through a second copy that waits again (dependencies/llama.cpp-f089c9c/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp, the eval callback's branch of the split computation). The wait is not part of the computation: the ranges of nodes and their order are what the card computes, and they can stay exactly as they are while the wait is taken once. That is the change here, in the scheduler alone, and it is the next step because it is the only part of a token's time that is neither the model's decode nor already measured as small.
repeating_pattern_check: Three things have happened more than once. (1) A faster way to read turned out to be another computation: thirty-two tokens at once (outputs apart by 1.3e-3 to 3.4e-3 of their size), the second card (9 of 30 answers worded differently), the torch forward (9 of 30). Why: the engine's kernels or their order differed between the two ways, and wording is decided by near ties. This change is built so that neither differs (the same ranges in the same order; only when the card is waited for), and it is not taken on that argument: every answer's four files are held by sha256 to the installed recorder's in the same run, and one file apart closes it whatever its time. (2) A time priced as arithmetic stood where a measurement was wanted, and was wrong: two recorders side by side were priced at 1.4 to 2.0 and measured at 0.72 (runs/recorders-beside-original/result.json); that run's capture was priced at 226 s and took 410.5 with its wait for the lock. Why: the parts on record did not include what the arrangement itself costs. Here the arithmetic leaves the same gap (what launching 212 ranges a token costs once nothing waits between them is in no record), so the prediction is stated as a range that includes no gain, and the two sides alternate call by call under one hold of the lock so that a wait for the card or another project's load is in neither side's seconds. (3) An instrument first ran on an engine inside an experiment and cost it (the reader of 11:03 AM CT November 14; the verifier's refusal at 3:31 AM CT November 15). This library runs on an engine here first, on the original, beside the installed one, and enters no capture, reading or protocol by this run.
what_went_wrong_before: Every construction so far repaired some answers and broke others, and the repeated correction on state values was stopped in its first pass. A step of a loop was 1 h 35 to 2 h in the on-policy loop and 44 to 52 minutes as the stopped loop's launcher stood; Marcos expects minutes. Under the gradient step Astra specified the capture is the largest part of a step, and the two measured attempts at its generation (the recorder's bookkeeping, recorders side by side) found no factor.
rule: Data roles: the thirty fitting answers of the cohort controlled-bf16-1 (tube.picks) and no others. The answers no fit uses are not generated, read or listed; the reserved folder is not opened. The model is the original file, read only. One step (`compare`), under one hold of card 0's lock: for each of the three calls of ten answers, in the selection's order, the recorder is run once as installed and once deferred, own_text.py's recorder call argument for argument; before every call the recorder, the two libraries and the comparison's own file are hashed and held to the sha256 this declaration names, and a file that is not the declared bytes starts no call; each process's library is read from its own map while it runs and held, by its inode, to the file hashed before its call, which is hashed again when the call has ended; a deferred process must also carry the scheduler's line in its log and an installed one must not; a call that did not run the declared library of its side ends the comparison there. Each answer's stream.f32, stream.jsonl, result.json and case.json are hashed, deferred against installed. A call's record is written first; then both streams of each answer whose four files are the same bytes are removed (the same command makes them again), and an answer with one file apart keeps both streams whole beside the record that names the files. A comparison is a count of equal bytes; no tolerance, threshold or score exists in this run. Nothing an answer says is compared or judged. The comparison is made once: what one that failed left is not touched. The research verifier runs before the step. The run writes only in its own folder. Whatever it finds, no instrument and no protocol is changed by it: the installed engine, the recorder and controlled-bf16-7 stay as they are, and a capture that uses the deferred library is a separate acceptance.

prediction.1_bytes: 30 of 30 answers' four files have the same sha256 on both sides. The patched scheduler computes the same ranges of nodes in the same order as the installed one; each wanted output is copied on the card's own queue right after the range that ends with it, so the copy is taken before any later node can reuse its memory; on the processor backend 18 of 18 wanted outputs were the installed path's bytes, 10 of them overwritten later in the same graph.
prediction.2_time: the installed side: about 15.6 ms a step, as nine answers stood alone in runs/recorders-beside-original (beside/beside-2.json: 75.5 s over their 4,844 steps, 14.6 to 16.7 ms answer by answer). The deferred side: between 9.3 and 15.0 ms a step, not known closer before it is measured. The lower end is the plain decode with its scores (7.9 ms) and the recorder's records and callbacks (1.4 to 1.6 ms; recorders-beside/bookkeeping.txt), if launching 212 ranges a token costs nothing once no wait stands between them. The upper end is the sham mode's 13.4 ms, which holds the launches and the waits together, with the records added, if the waits were never the cost and the launches are. No record separates the two.

would_weaken_it: Nothing here bears on the hypothesis. On the instrument: (1) one file of one answer with other bytes on the deferred side means a copy taken on the card's queue is not the output the installed stop reads (work on another queue, or memory reused before the copy): the deferred read-back is another computation as far as the record goes and is closed whatever its time; both streams are kept. (2) A deferred side that is not faster (the median of an answer's deferred seconds over its installed seconds at or above 1) means the waits are not what a kept token pays for: the lever is closed with its number, and what is left is the ranges themselves, which only a change of how the engine builds and allocates its graph removes.

Reported: the milliseconds a step on each side (the seconds of the answers that have seconds on both sides, over their steps), the median, least and most of an answer's deferred seconds over its installed seconds, and each call's whole seconds on each side. It is a measurement, not a gate: no value of it starts or stops anything in this run

staging_chunk.derivation: 64 MiB of host memory a chunk in the patched scheduler: the most one split's wanted outputs take is the prefill's microbatch, which that record gives as 32 tokens at once, times the 212 kept outputs, each 1,536 float32 wide: 41.7 MB, and 64 MiB is the next power of two above it. It bounds nothing: an output larger than what is left of a chunk takes the next chunk, and one larger than a chunk gets a chunk of its own size, so no byte of any output depends on it
staging_chunk.scales_with: the microbatch, the model's width and the kept outputs

Nothing else of the run is changed: the patch, the library, the answers, the order and the comparison of bytes are as declared.
